title: Stretch: Complex Actions
welcome_lead: Push yourself — analyse multi-joint actions and antagonistic muscle pairs.
meta_desc: GCSE PE Movement Analysis stretch: complex actions and antagonistic pairs.
final_note: Outstanding! You can now break down any sporting action into its components.

concepts.def: Muscle that contracts to produce movement (prime mover).
Muscle that relaxes as agonist contracts.
Two muscles working in opposition (e.g. biceps/triceps).
Muscle contracts without changing length (a plank).
Circular movement at a ball-and-socket joint.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Muscles work in pairs because they can only pull, not push. Key pairs:

  • Biceps / triceps at the elbow.
  • Quadriceps / hamstrings at the knee.
  • Hip flexors / gluteals at the hip.
  • Gastrocnemius / tibialis anterior at the ankle.

Isotonic contractions change muscle length and create movement, with two sub-types: concentric (shortening, lifting curl) and eccentric (lengthening, lowering curl). Isometric means same length — a wall sit or rugby scrum.
The shooting arm uses elbow extension (triceps agonist), shoulder flexion (deltoids), in the sagittal plane around the transverse axis. The follow-through wrist flick adds spin.
